title: ReleaseHarnessDraft
description: A mutable proposal for a contract, together with the open questions it has not settled. A draft is allowed to be incomplete -- that is what distinguishes it from an accepted contract -- so this schema constrains shape without demanding resolution.

proposition.description: The proposed contract. Deliberately NOT validated against contract-v1 here: a draft may be missing pieces a contract must have, and validating it as a contract would force an author to fake completeness before they have it.

expect.description: What must hold. Deliberately unconstrained HERE: the shape is determined by `kind` and enforced by the allOf rules below, which close it per kind. See assertion-kinds-v1.json.

supported_by.description: Ids of claims in the authoring record that this assertion rests on. Acceptance refuses any assertion whose cited claims do not support a claim.

allOf.description: An assertion of kind "http" may only expect what the http adapter reads.

expect.description: Exercise an HTTP endpoint. WHERE it lives is an execution binding; this says only what must be true of the response.

path.description: Path appended to the bound location. Defaults to /.

body_contains.description: Substring that must appear in the response body. D39: the real transfer test found the highest-value proposition available -- that the deployed service is running the revision intended for this release -- unwritable, because the service exposes it in the body and this kind could only read a status code. A substring test is the smallest primitive that closes it; anything richer is a query language, which this is deliberately not.

allOf.description: An assertion of kind "cli" may only expect what the cli adapter reads.

expect.description: Exercise a command. WHAT is executed comes from the execution binding -- an assertion never carries a command, because a command is a local fact about where things are installed, not part of a promise.

args.description: Extra arguments appended to the bound command.

stdout_contains.description: Substring that must appear in stdout.

stderr_contains.description: Substring that must appear in stderr. D40: well-behaved CLIs put diagnostics on stderr, so "the validator refuses for the expected reason" degraded to an exit-code check that any unrelated crash could satisfy. Note the distinction this preserves: stderr may be ASSERTED by an author who chose the expectation, but it is still never READ to attribute a cause -- the thing removed from the trust boundary was the harness guessing from stderr, not an author promising about it.

questions.description: What the author could not settle. A blocking question must be resolved before acceptance; a non-blocking one is recorded and may stay open, because an author who is penalised for recording uncertainty will stop recording it.

resolution.description: The operator's answer. Requires `resolved_by`: a resolution nobody is named for is indistinguishable from an agent answering its own question, which the protocol forbids and the artifact could not previously evidence.

resolved_by.description: Who decided. Attribution, not authorization -- an agent may record an operator's answer, but it must say whose answer it is.

resolved_at.description: When, ISO 8601. Optional, and never part of proposition identity.
